shortcuts.title: Shortcuts & commands

tester.desc: Click here, then press something. You see exactly what Pauli Speaks' keyboard hook sees. Shortcuts pause while you test.
shortcuts.more.title: More ways to start
shortcuts.more.desc: For pedals, Stream Deck, mice and scripts.
shortcuts.more.doubleTap.title: Double-tap a modifier
shortcuts.more.doubleTap.desc: Press Add above, then tap Ctrl, Alt or Shift twice quickly - within 0.4 s, nothing else pressed. A double-tap always toggles.
shortcuts.more.pedals.title: Foot pedals and macro keys
shortcuts.more.pedals.desc: Set the pedal or Stream Deck key to send F13-F24: no app uses them. A pedal that sends press and release separately works as Hold.
shortcuts.more.mouse.title: Mouse buttons
shortcuts.more.mouse.desc: Middle click and the side buttons work as shortcuts, but they still do their usual job too (Back, Forward) - Windows doesn't let Pauli Speaks block them yet.
shortcuts.more.links.title: Links and command line
shortcuts.more.links.desc: Point Stream Deck, AutoHotkey, foot-pedal software or a script at these. Links can only start and stop dictation, because any web page can open a link; pasting and key presses need the command line.
voice.title: Voice commands
voice.sub: Say these while dictating. Add your own in any language.
voice.desc: Line breaks and snippets work anywhere. Actions like "send it" only count at the very start or end, so "I'll send it tomorrow" stays as text.
files.title: Transcribe a file
files.sub: Audio or video - voice memos, lectures, meetings, interviews. Runs on this PC like dictation.
files.formats: mp3, m4a, wav, ogg, flac, webm, mp4, mov…
dictionary.sub: Teach Pauli Speaks your words, and give it shortcuts for text you type a lot.
dictionary.desc: Names, brands and jargon. They're also given to Whisper as hints, so it hears them right the first time.
snippets.title: Snippets
snippets.desc: Say the trigger phrase and the full text is typed instead - your email, address, signature, a standard reply.

command.desc: Select text anywhere, hold {keys} and say what to do: "make this more formal", "translate to German", "turn this into a bulleted list". With nothing selected it writes new text for you. Uses a free Groq API key (set under Speech recognition → Cloud API).

privacy.recovery.title: Recover dictation after a crash

backup.title: Backup
backup.export.title: Export settings
backup.export.desc: Saves your shortcuts, voice commands, dictionary, snippets and app styles to a file. API keys are never included.
backup.import.title: Import settings
backup.import.desc: Loads those settings from a backup file. They replace the ones you have now.
update.title: Updates
update.beta.title: Get early versions
update.beta.desc: Try new versions before everyone else (pre-releases on GitHub). They may have rough edges, and you still get every regular release.
diagnostics.title: Something not working?
diagnostics.desc: Copies diagnostic info (versions, settings, the last 100 log lines) and opens a bug report on GitHub. Paste it there. It never contains what you dictated or your API key.
about.how.title: How it works
about.how.1: A low-level keyboard hook watches for your shortcut in any app. It never blocks or records other keys.
about.how.2: While you hold it, the microphone is recorded at 16 kHz.
about.how.3: When you let go, Whisper turns speech into text on your own CPU, so nothing leaves your PC.
about.how.4: Optionally the text is translated: Whisper's built-in translator (fast, English) or NLLB-200 (best, 30+ languages).
about.how.5: Fillers, voice commands and your dictionary are applied, then the text is pasted with Ctrl+V and your clipboard is put back.
about.how.details: Shortcuts use exact key-combination matching, a 500 ms tap / double-tap window, hands-free lock, Esc to cancel and Start-menu masking for Ctrl+Win.
about.licence.title: Licence
about.licence.desc: Pauli Speaks is free and open source (MIT). It is built on open-source components and downloads open models; NLLB-200, used for {best} translation, is licensed for non-commercial use only.
